planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring once frost danger passes; propagate from semi-hardwood cuttings in summer.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in full sun to light shade in well-drained to seasonally moist soil; this Western Australian hybrid, raised at Kings Park and Botanic Garden in Perth, combines the vigor of Callistemon citrinus with denser, more floriferous crimson flower spikes carried on gently weeping branches. It tolerates boggy or periodically flooded ground as well as poor, sandy soils, making it unusually adaptable for a bottlebrush. Masses of nectar-rich red brushes open mainly in spring and summer and draw hummingbirds and other nectar feeders. Use it as an informal screen, clipped hedge, or specimen shrub in low-water coastal and inland landscapes.
sources: Kings Park and Botanic Garden (Western Australia)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Set out rooted cuttings in full sun in well-drained soil; 'Captain Cook' is a naturally dwarf, densely weeping selection of the normally tree-sized weeping bottlebrush, reaching roughly a third the size of the species. Narrow, pendulous branches are tipped with bright red brush-shaped flower spikes chiefly in mid to late spring, with occasional rebloom in late summer and fall. It withstands moderate frost better than many bottlebrush selections and suits smaller gardens, large containers, or low hedges where the species' mature tree form would be impractical. Originally marketed as 'Compacta', it was renamed to mark the 1970 bicentenary of Cook's voyage to Australia.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Ruby Glow New Zealand Tea Tree

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in lean, sharply drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun.

directions: Grow in full sun in lean, acidic, sharply drained soil; 'Ruby Glow' is a double-flowered New Zealand tea tree cultivar bearing saucer-shaped, deep ruby-red blooms with darker centers that smother the fine, needle-like foliage from spring into summer. Foliage deepens to a coppery bronze through fall and winter, adding cool-season color even without flowers. Like other manuka cultivars it is intolerant of heavy or waterlogged soil and should be grown in a peaty, well-aerated mix if containerized. Light pruning immediately after bloom keeps plants dense without sacrificing the following year's flower display.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun, ideally in a coastal or mild-winter garden.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil, ideally in a coastal or mild-winter garden; 'Tahiti' is a dwarf sport of the New Zealand Christmas tree, mounding to only about a yard high and wide with the same silvery new growth and crimson, bottlebrush-like flowers of the full-size species in miniature. Its naturally compact, bushy habit needs little pruning to stay neat, unlike seedling pohutukawa that must be sheared hard to control. Once established it shares the species' outstanding tolerance of salt spray, coastal wind, and drought. The small scale makes it a practical choice for pots, low hedges, and borders where a standard pohutukawa would quickly outgrow the space.
sources: Royal New Zealand Institute of Horticulture

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or started plants after frost danger has passed, in full sun in well-drained soil.

directions: Start from cuttings or purchase started plants and set out after frost danger has passed, in full sun and well-drained soil; 'Santa Anita' is a selection of blue daisy bred for noticeably larger flowerheads, up to about 2 inches across, on a tidier, more compact mound than the species. The sky-blue, yellow-centered daisies appear over a long summer-to-fall season and are especially effective massed in containers or at the front of a border. It shares the species' preference for cool to moderate temperatures and may flower less in the height of summer heat. Shear lightly after bloom flushes to encourage repeat flowering and maintain its compact shape.

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown stock in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in full sun to light shade in lean, well-drained soil; 'Jervis Gem' is a compact selection of coastal rosemary, derived from the larger 'Wynyabbie Gem', that forms a dense, rounded mound of soft grey-green foliage to around 4 feet tall and wide. Small mauve to pale blue flowers are produced almost continuously through the year in mild climates. It shares the species' outstanding tolerance of salt spray, wind, and drought, and its naturally tidy habit makes it well suited to low hedging, topiary, and container culture with minimal shearing. Avoid heavy, poorly drained soils, which can lead to root problems.
